title: CONTEST-018-contest-support-playbook
universal_lens: Contest support playbook formalizes a constrained state-transition system where legal-compliance boundaries gate transitions from specification to execution. The duplicate-gate isomorphism maps extension relations to dependency DAGs, while risk-level MEDIUM induces a hard veto on prize/deposit/leaderboard activation without founder-legal sign-off. Fake-data-first implementation enforces a simulation-before-deployment manifold.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats contest eligibility, scoring, and disputes as latent variables with conformal prediction sets calibrated on fake-data simulations. Bayesian prior over legal-risk MEDIUM yields posterior veto probability ≈1 for paid flows absent explicit approval. Responsible-play constraints map to conformal coverage guarantees on user-harm metrics. Scoring disputes resolve via posterior predictive checks against ground-truth rules.
gse_mapping: GSE models contest lifecycle as a finite-state machine: {VERIFY_CLONE, READ_DOCS, BUILD_SPECS, MOCK_DATA, AWAIT_APPROVAL, LAUNCH}. Legal boundary defines absorbing veto states for {PAID_CONTESTS, PRIZES, DEPOSITS, LIVE_LEADERBOARDS, GEOFENCING}. Duplicate gate enforces parent-child DAG consistency via extension relation. Implementation plan sequences transitions with fake-data checkpoint as mandatory intermediate state.

primitives.name: Legal-Compliance Veto Gate Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Do not launch paid contests, prizes, entry fees, live leaderboards, geofenced eligibility, or user deposits without founder/legal approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: s: system state (dimensionless); \mathcal{S}_{\text{paid}}: subset of states with paid contests/prizes/fees/leaderboards/geofencing/deposits (dimensionless); Approval: binary predicate (dimensionless); \mathcal{V}_{\text{legal}}: veto signal {0,1} (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Founder/legal approval is a well-defined binary predicate; paid contest features are enumerable and mutually exclusive from free/mock modes; veto is irreversible without explicit approval.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Approval predicate becomes ambiguous (e.g., verbal vs written); jurisdiction changes alter \mathcal{S}_{\text{paid}} definition; emergency overrides bypass gate.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE absorbing veto states in contest FSM; isomorphic to GSI conformal veto where coverage guarantee fails if paid features activate without approval.
layer2.telemetry: Veto activation count; approval latency; false-positive veto rate on mock flows.

primitives.name: Duplicate-Gate Extension Isomorphism
primitives.verbatim_quote: # CONTEST-018: Contest support playbook ## Duplicate Gate duplicate_check_status: EXTENSION matched_existing_ids: BUILD-GV2-034, BUILD-GV2-038 relation_to_existing: Child extension of existing growth-os-v2 contest/community work.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: C_{new}: new contest card (dimensionless); \mathcal{P}: set of parent cards {BUILD-GV2-034, BUILD-GV2-038} (dimensionless); \prec: child-extension partial order (dimensionless); disputes, scoring, eligibility, responsible-play: feature-set predicates (dimensionless); \mathcal{E}: classification {EXTENSION, DUPLICATE} (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Parent cards form a DAG; feature-set predicates are decidable; extension requires non-empty novel feature union.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Feature predicates overlap ambiguously; parent DAG has cycles; novel features exist but are undocumented.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE dependency DAG validation; maps to GSI prior over contest-format space where extension implies non-zero KL divergence from parent posterior.
layer2.telemetry: Extension classification accuracy; feature-novelty score; DAG cycle detection rate.

primitives.name: Fake-Data-First Implementation Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: parent_id: BUILD-GV2-034 dependency_ids: none ## Goal Create a safe, docs-first or fake-data-first implementation packet for Contest support playbook.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S_{spec}: specification state (dimensionless); S_{mock}: mock/fake-data state (dimensionless); \phi_{spec}: specification predicates (dimensionless); live_data: predicate for production data (dimensionless); Approval_{impl}: implementation approval predicate (dimensionless); S_{prod}: production state (dimensionless); \mathcal{T}_{\text{fake}}: transition operator (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Specification predicates are formalizable; fake data can satisfy all predicates; approval is a discrete gate; no side effects in mock state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Specification predicates require live data (e.g., geofencing); fake data cannot stress-test scaling; approval predicate never triggers.

layer2.mapping: GSE mandatory intermediate state in contest FSM; GSI prior predictive simulation where fake data generates synthetic likelihood for conformal calibration before live exposure.
layer2.telemetry: Mock-to-prod transition rate; predicate coverage on fake data; approval latency distribution.

primitives.name: Acceptance Criteria Absorbing State
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Acceptance Criteria - No production code or live contest launched.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: system state (dimensionless); ProductionCode: predicate for deployed production code (dimensionless); LiveContest: predicate for active contest with real users (dimensionless); \mathcal{S}_{\text{accept}}: accepting state set (dimensionless); \mathcal{A}: acceptance indicator {0,1} (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: ProductionCode and LiveContest are observable and mutually exclusive with acceptance; no partial credit.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Shadow launches blur LiveContest definition; production code exists but feature-flagged off; acceptance criteria evolve post-hoc.

layer2.mapping: GSE absorbing state in contest FSM preventing LAUNCH transition; GSI conformal guarantee that test-set coverage holds only if no live contamination.
layer2.telemetry: Acceptance state dwell time; production-code detection false negatives; live-contest leakage events.

reasoning_traces.think:
The playbook defines a constrained transition system where legal risk MEDIUM induces a hard veto gate (legal_veto_gate) on any state containing paid contests, prizes, entry fees, live leaderboards, geofenced eligibility, or user deposits. This veto is isomorphic to an absorbing barrier in the GSE contest FSM: states in \mathcal{S}_{paid} transition to a veto sink unless Approval(founder,legal)=1. The duplicate gate (duplicate_extension_gate) enforces DAG consistency by classifying CONTEST-018 as EXTENSION iff it adds non-empty novel features (disputes, scoring, eligibility, responsible-play) over parents BUILD-GV2-034/038. This maps to GSI as a prior over contest-format space where extension implies KL(p_new||p_parent)>0. The fake-data-first transition (fake_data_first_transition) mandates a simulation manifold S_mock satisfying all spec predicates \phi_{spec} without live data, acting as a mandatory intermediate state before production. This is a derived kernel: GSI uses fake data for prior predictive conformal calibration; GSE enforces it as a checkpoint. The acceptance criteria (acceptance_criteria_absorbing) defines an absorbing state \mathcal{S}_{accept} where ProductionCode=0 and LiveContest=0, preventing LAUNCH. Dualities: veto gate ↔ conformal coverage failure; extension gate ↔ KL divergence; fake-data transition ↔ prior predictive simulation; acceptance ↔ test-set purity. Failure modes: approval ambiguity breaks veto; feature overlap breaks extension; live-data dependence breaks fake-data manifold; shadow launches break acceptance.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Legal veto gates descend from regulatory compliance frameworks (SOX, GDPR) formalized as absorbing barriers in finite-state machines. Duplicate extension gates derive from DAG-based dependency resolution in build systems (Bazel, Nix) and version-control merge strategies. Fake-data-first transitions originate in simulation-based verification (model checking, digital twins) and privacy-preserving ML (synthetic data). Acceptance absorbing states trace to formal methods (invariant checking) and CI/CD gatekeeping.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Founder/legal acts as a high-threshold approval oracle with veto power; their utility function prioritizes risk avoidance over speed. Contest participants (latent) seek prize eligibility and leaderboard status, creating pressure to bypass veto. Engineers (implementers) optimize for mock-state completeness to accelerate approval. Compliance auditors (external) verify veto gate integrity and acceptance criteria adherence. Adversarial actors probe geofencing/eligibility boundaries to exploit fake-data gaps.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity: legal veto must not correlate with fake-data completeness (otherwise mock quality becomes approval proxy). Leakage veto: no live user data, PII, or real-money flows in S_mock; conformal sets calibrated on fake data must not leak into production priors. Extension gate must not share feature predicates with veto gate (disputes/scoring ≤ paid features). Acceptance state must be reachable only via fake-data transition, not via veto bypass.
